exercise.name: Dumbbell Seated Kickback

reference.title: Dumbbell Seated Kickback
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

secondaryBodyParts: Shoulders and upper back (holding the arm back)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you straighten the arms back, breathe in as the forearms swing down.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, short squeeze, about 2 s back

prescription.load: User-chosen light dumbbells; kickbacks need much less weight than presses
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, then heavier dumbbells

cues.text: Sit on the end of a bench, feet flat. Lean forward from the hips with a long back; upper arms along the sides of the trunk, elbows bent about 90 degrees, dumbbells hanging below the elbows, palms facing in.
Breathe out and straighten both elbows, pushing the dumbbells back until the arms are straight.
Squeeze the backs of the arms; the upper arms stay where they are.
Breathe in and let the forearms swing slowly back to hanging.
Keep the lean and the upper arms still; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the upper arms to move the dumbbells
mistakes.fix: Pin the upper arms beside the trunk; only the elbows move.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to lean forward
mistakes.fix: Hinge at the hips with a long spine and the chest open.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the upper arms drop as the arms tire
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows up at back level; use lighter dumbbells.
Take about two seconds to lower.

kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees (forearm hanging) to straight (clinical opinion); kickbacks scored high for triceps EMG in the ACE study (Boehler 2011)
Upper arm held back along the trunk, at low shoulder elevation (Kholinne 2018)
Leaning well forward from the hips, back long (clinical opinion)
The dumbbells pass beside the hips and above the bench (clinical opinion)
Slow, with a pause at full extension (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #964, Dumbbell Seated Kickback, video (movement reference only; page not read)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)

Boehler, Porcari, Kline, Hendrix and Foster, ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises (American Council on Exercise; University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, 15 trained women, triceps EMG relative to the triangle push-up)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The forward lean loads the low back: keep it long and the dumbbells light.
modify: Low-back discomfort: do one arm at a time with the other hand on the knee, or use the bench-supported kickback.
Shoulder discomfort at the back: let the upper arms sit a little lower.
regressions: One-arm kickback with a hand and knee on the bench.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the dumbbell, hardest near full extension; kickbacks gave some of the highest triceps EMG in the ACE comparison (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the dumbbell, hardest near full extension; kickbacks gave some of the highest triceps EMG in the ACE comparison (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm back along the trunk.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm back along the trunk.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk in the lean.
